- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+ levels) — model reacts too aggressively, then corrects too late.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — fails to recognize downward drift after peaks.
- Tends to underestimate true volatility in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window.
- Shows persistent bias toward higher prices in the first 10 days of the forecast, then gradually adjusts downward — suggests lag in capturing short-term momentum.
- Often misses the true low point in the 30-day window, especially when prices drop sharply mid-period.
- Forecast mean is typically 1–2% higher than true mean, indicating a systematic upward bias.
- Model underestimates the impact of seasonal or event-driven price drops (e.g., after policy announcements or market corrections).
